extracted.intended_audience: researchers and developers building NLP tools for peer review; conference organizers, program chairs, meta-reviewers, and policy-makers interested in automating or analyzing peer-review workflows
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and applying NLP tools to support stages of conference-style peer review (reviews, author responses, discussions, meta-reviews, decisions, revisions, and post-review analysis), while accounting for data, privacy, and legal constraints. Focuses on information aggregation, summarization, notification, editing support, and large-scale analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-document mapping of author responses to reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and give reviewers clear pointers to the parts of the manuscript under discussion by mapping author responses to review reports and manuscript text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cross-document analysis to highlight parts of the response that address reviewers’ criticisms and report changes in submission text in response to the review (e.g., Kuznetsov et al., 2022; Kennard et al., 2022). This aids discussion and focused evaluation of whether responses correspond to claimed edits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detecting participant-relevant updates and selective notifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Detect updates to a conversation that concern each participant and notify them accordingly, to avoid overwhelming or insufficient notifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic NLP can identify which updates are relevant to which participant (explicit replies are insufficient; notifying everyone is overwhelming). Tools should balance coverage and signal-to-noise when sending notifications about discussion updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flagging mandatory intervention scenarios for meta-reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Notify meta-reviewers when their intervention is mandatory, e.g., open conflict between reviewers and authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NLP tools can detect disputes or escalation in discussions (inspired by dispute-tactic work) and prompt meta-reviewer action rather than relying on participants to self-identify conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detecting anchoring and herding effects among reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Track and flag influence of reviewers toward each other (anchoring/herding), which can distort independent assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze discussion structures and subsequent changes in review reports to identify disproportionate influence or follow-the-initiator effects (Teplitskiy et al., 2019; Stelmakh et al., 2023a). Flagging such patterns can help preserve independence of judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personalized reminders to increase reviewer participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use NLP to generate personalized reminders and pre-filled templates to nudge reviewers to engage in discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personalized reminders are generally more effective than generic ones but require effort; NLP can draft customized reminder emails for meta-reviewers to finalize. Deeper assistance can detect unanswered items requiring follow-up and prompt reviewers accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detecting unresolved reviewer concerns and score non-updates
rubrics_metrics.description: Automatically detect cases where a reviewer raised a concern, authors addressed it, but the reviewer did not adjust their score or follow through.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NLP can find reviewer statements that go unanswered or where fixes are acknowledged but scores remain low; detecting such cases while reviewers are still present can improve fairness and reduce later appeals to meta-reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-review aggregation responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Aggregate individual reviews and discussions, detect low-quality reviews, find emergency reviewers, and provide a grounded meta-review and recommendation for PCs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meta-reviewers must read reviews, rebuttals, and discussions and aggregate them into strengths, weaknesses, required changes, and an acceptance recommendation. NLP assistance should facilitate multi-document analysis but not fully replace human judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aspect-based analysis of reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Separate peer reviews into statements and categorize them by argumentative/pragmatic function and by aspects (strengths, weaknesses, technical soundness, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aspect-based analysis helps meta-reviewers detect insufficiently covered aspects (e.g., lack of evaluation). Finer-grained, contribution-type-dependent aspect labels (dataset papers vs experimental papers) are suggested to improve detection of missing scrutiny areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-review summarization requirements (self-consistency, faithfulness, engagement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Summaries of reviews/discussions should list contributions, weaknesses, and a summary of discussion while accounting for reviewer confidence and expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checklist-based prompting of LLMs has been used to write summaries that fulfill meta-review requirements of self-consistency, faithfulness, and active engagement (Zeng et al., 2023). Summaries must resolve conflicts and reflect inter-document relationships; current models struggle with conflict resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid full automation for high-stakes meta-reviewing
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not fully automate meta-review composition or decision-making given high stakes and current NLP limitations and ethical concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NLP may support meta-reviewers but should not replace expert human judgment; systems should be used to augment, not substitute, human decision-makers (ethical caution referenced).

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-review writing quality criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Meta-reviews must be clear, well-substantiated, include strengths, weaknesses, required improvements, take an unequivocal stance, and prioritize required changes when conditioning acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply similar writing-assistance tools as for reviews (clarity/substantiation), plus hedging/uncertainty detection and prioritization. Meta-reviews serve decision-making, so they should state a clear recommendation and identify conditions for acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group borderline papers by similarity for consistent decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Cluster borderline papers by topic, contribution type, strengths and weaknesses to aid PCs in consistent ranking and comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NLP can group papers and generate clusters of decisions so PCs can compare similar submissions and reduce cases where comparable papers receive inconsistent outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pairwise comparisons and aggregated-contribution ranking for tie-breaking
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilitate pairwise paper and review comparison by aggregating individual contributions based on review reports and meta-reviews to break ties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use aggregation of reviewers' textual comments and meta-reviews to provide side-by-side comparisons of contributions when decisions require tie-breaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-review score calibration and strictness scoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare and calibrate meta-review scores/comments to reduce unintended/unfair assessments and provide a strictness score for meta-reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply techniques analogous to reviewer score calibration to meta-reviews; provide PCs with meta-reviewer strictness metrics to inform ranking and scaling decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detect large meta-reviewer/reviewer disagreements as potential misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Flag papers where meta-reviewer stance significantly departs from reviewers' assessments, as this may indicate bias or unethical meta-reviewing (e.g., collusion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use NLP to detect significant disagreements and surface them for careful human evaluation by PCs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support editorial priorities via natural-language ranking criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow PCs to specify editorial priorities in natural language and use NLP to rank borderline papers according to those priorities using manuscripts and review texts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'rank papers based on the largest disagreement in overall assessment, then relevance to special theme'—NLP systems should adapt on the fly to text-based ranking instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automated augmentation of best-paper nomination pools
rubrics_metrics.description: Augment reviewer nominations/high-score lists by detecting papers with similar positive comments about novelty, soundness, and contributions, and detect innovative/unique work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use comment similarity and methods for innovation detection (Hofstra et al., 2020) to build a more inclusive candidate pool for best-paper committees, compensating for scarce reviewer nominations or calibration issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision assistance: edit localization and suggestion
rubrics_metrics.description: Localize requested edits by connecting reviews and rebuttals to manuscript text, suggest edits, and help execute some revisions while honoring author control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NLP approaches can align comments to sentences/paragraphs and propose edits, but automation should be conservative since edits range from typos to new experiments. Prioritization and routing between assistants and humans, and respecting page limits and formatting, are key.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision analysis: coverage, new material, and edit intent labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze revisions to check whether they address reviewer points and rebuttal promises, detect newly added material not previously reviewed, align revisions at sentence/paragraph level, and label edits by intent (grammar, clarity, factual adjustment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use diff-like and alignment tools for manuscript versions; detect changes that materially alter content and require re-review; support both manuscript-level and collection-level analysis (e.g., to evaluate policy interventions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-review analysis: identify reviewer trends and biases
rubrics_metrics.description: Aggregate reviews to identify trends, biases, and correlations (e.g., which reviewer requests correlate with acceptance) to inform reviewer guidance and policy changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large-scale NLP analysis can reveal problematic or consistent patterns in reviewing; share such insights to help authors avoid pitfalls and to inform reviewer training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze which discussion forms influence meta-reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine what forms of discussion and which aspects of discourse most influence meta-review decisions and why people adjust their reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggregate reviews, discussions, and meta-reviews to analyze influence patterns; use argumentative-structure analyses to correlate discussion features with meta-review outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate peer-review predictive validity (impact forecasting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether peer-review can predict future impact of the work by relating reviewer impact assessments to later metrics such as citations (optionally refined by citation type/class).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use citation counts and refined citation types (background vs method citations) as imperfect but informative impact proxies; correlate early reviewer judgments with these metrics to evaluate reviewing effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic analysis of free-text survey responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Use clustering or topic-extraction NLP tools to analyze open-ended survey responses from reviewers to surface trends and feedback efficiently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structured survey fields are easy to aggregate; free text requires NLP to reveal common issues and attitudes, aiding policy adjustments and community feedback loops.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve multimodal, structured, and interconnected peer-review data
rubrics_metrics.description: When collecting peer-reviewing datasets, preserve as much information as possible including manuscript original formats, non-textual elements (figures, tables, formulas), structure, categorical metadata, and numerical scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The richness and inter-connectedness of peer-review data (reviews, rebuttals, discussions, meta-reviews) provide supervision signals; losing structure (e.g., manuscript layout or form fields) reduces utility for downstream tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data availability strategies and representativeness trade-offs
rubrics_metrics.description: Handle scarcity of open peer-review data via three strategies: use closed data (with access restrictions), rely on open data from select venues (potentially unrepresentative), or collect donation-based data (time-consuming but flexible).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each strategy has trade-offs for reproducibility, representativeness, licensing, and administrative burden. Quantify differences between open samples and full populations using aggregate statistics when releasing data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informed consent and GDPR-like personal-data safeguards
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain informed consent and clearly state what data is collected, purposes, storage, withdrawal options, and take into account GDPR/personal-data requirements when collecting peer-review data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research use is more permissive under GDPR than commercial use but still requires careful consent handling. Use opt-in/opt-out workflows and clear documentation of data handling policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensing and intellectual-property considerations for peer-review data
rubrics_metrics.description: Associate peer-reviewing data with licenses that regulate downstream use; decide attribution, confidentiality, data ownership, distribution responsibilities, and repository/storage choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer-reviewing data often mixes contributions by multiple parties and may fall into licensing grey zones. Explicit license agreements and consent forms are necessary to permit open research use and redistribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cautious use of third-party/off-site processing for closed data
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid processing closed or not-yet-open peer-reviewing data off-site (e.g., using closed-source LLM APIs) without careful consideration of licenses, consent, and confidentiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Off-site processing raises ethical and legal concerns; ensure license/consent permits such processing and that confidentiality and data protection obligations are satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Yes-Yes-Yes workflow for opt-in data collection (example)
rubrics_metrics.description: A three-step opt-in workflow where (1) reviewers consent and transfer a CC non-commercial license for reviews, (2) PCs accept the paper (paper appears in proceedings), and (3) authors consent to data being made public — only then is data released.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ACL Rolling Review example (NLPeer corpus) automates selective publication of peer-review data only for accepted papers with consent from reviewers and authors. It demonstrates practical implementation of consent, licensing, and automation for data collection.
